summary: A local news piece covering the Multicultural Festival held September 15-17, 2023, themed "Embracing Diversity in Our Community." It describes the parade, music, dance and theater, global food, kids' activities, art exhibit, lectures, marketplace, traditional sports, fashion runway and closing ceremony. The article presents the festival as a cornerstone of the community's identity and a celebration of inclusiveness.
one_line: Report on the September 15-17, 2023 Multicultural Festival, with its parade, performances, food, art, lectures, markets, sports, fashion and closing ceremony celebrating community diversity.
key_facts: The Multicultural Festival ran from September 15 to September 17, 2023.
The 2023 festival theme was "Embracing Diversity in Our Community."
The festival opened with a grand parade on the morning of September 15, led by community leader Maria Gonzalez and Mayor Johnathan Li, who also performed the ribbon-cutting.
The Cultural Music Pavilion featured Korean drummers, Mexican Mariachi bands, classical Indian dancers and Russian ballet.
The "Theater of the World," curated by Richard Emerson, presented African folklore, Japanese Noh theater and Italian opera.
At the Festival Food Court, chef Aisha Patel demonstrated Indian cuisine and Chef Paolo Rossi demonstrated making fresh pasta.

The Kids' Corner offered language taster sessions, storytelling, and craft tents where children made traditional masks and toys from recycled materials; Stephen O’Malley ran face painting and eco-friendly art lessons.
The Art and Photography Exhibit had the theme "Unity in Diversity," and Elena Rodriguez showed her "Faces of Our Town" portrait collection.
The lecture series at the community center featured Dr. Samuel Okeke, a Nigerian anthropologist, and Lisa Chang, a Korean-American historian, on cultural identity, immigration and multiculturalism.
In the Marketplace, Carlos Moreno's Aztec-inspired silverwork and Fatimah Al-Hassan's hand-embroidered hijabs drew particular attention.
The Traditional Sports and Games Pavilion featured Irish hurling, Korean taekwondo demonstrations and the Chinese game Go.
The Fashion Fusion Runway included designers Habibah Abubakar, who mixed African prints with high street trends, and David Lee, who drew on historical European attire.
The closing ceremony included performances, fireworks and an all-inclusive dance circle.
